case_metadata.policy_pathway: Section 2 — General coverage criteria, B. Reauthorization
plan_variant_evidence: Denial letter plan line: 'Commercial employer group pharmacy benefit (fully insured, Ohio)'
Denial letter cites Section 2, not Section 3
case_metadata.design_note: The third misstated-threshold case, and the one where the correct figure is easiest to miss. This reauthorization subsection lists four response limbs in sequence — 3 percent for Qsymia, 4 percent for Saxenda, 5 percent for Wegovy, 5 percent for all other appetite suppressants. The denial applied the last, most general limb to a drug that has its own named limb two lines above it.

derived_values.name: weight_reduction_from_treatment_start
derived_values.note: 227 to 217 lb is 10 lb, or 4.4 percent. Above the 4 percent Saxenda reauthorization threshold; below the 5 percent figure the denial asserts.

denial_ground_truth.denial_reason_text: Reauthorization requires a weight loss of 5 percent or more of baseline body weight; the documented reduction is 4.4 percent.
denial_ground_truth.cited_policy_reference: UnitedHealthcare Pharmacy, Clinical Pharmacy Programs — Prior Authorization/Notification - Plans with Weight Loss/Appetite Suppression Medication Coverage (Program Number 2026 P 1114-20, effective 5/1/2026), Section 2, Coverage Criteria, B. Reauthorization
denial_ground_truth.cited_requirement_text: Weight loss of ≥ 5% of baseline body weight for all other appetite suppressants

misstatement.denial_asserts: weight loss of 5 percent or more of baseline body weight
misstatement.policy_actually_requires_text: Weight loss of ≥ 4% of baseline body weight for Saxenda
misstatement.explanation: The 5 percent figure comes from the catch-all limb for 'all other appetite suppressants'. Saxenda is not an 'other' product here: it has its own named limb requiring 4 percent, two lines earlier in the same subsection.

policy_ground_truth.policy_name: Prior Authorization/Notification - Plans with Weight Loss/Appetite Suppression Medication Coverage

criteria.requirement: For Saxenda, weight loss of 4 percent or more of baseline body weight.
criteria.policy_support_text: Weight loss of ≥ 4% of baseline body weight for Saxenda

scope_notes: The reauthorization response criterion is a list of alternatives, one of which must be met. The limbs are drug-specific: 3 percent for Qsymia, 4 percent for Saxenda, 5 percent for Wegovy injection or tablet, and 5 percent for all other appetite suppressants. A drug with its own named limb is not an 'other' product.
The reauthorization section does not re-apply the initial-authorization BMI, age or indication criteria.

evidence_ground_truth.evidence_timing_note: The 2026-05-04 note was submitted and reviewed. The payer computed the percentage correctly from it.

expected_evidence.evidence_text: 227 lb on 11/10/2025 annotated 'recorded on the day liraglutide was started' and 217 lb on 05/04/2026. The reduction is 10 lb, or 4.4 percent of baseline, above the 4 percent Saxenda threshold.
expected_evidence.evidence_location: OBJECTIVE section, weights on file; TREATMENT COURSE

expected_evidence.evidence_text: Dietitian input from 10/13/2025, before treatment start, with monthly reviews continuing to date; twice-weekly swimming and Thursday bowls. Plan item 1 continues all three.

per_criterion.reason: A 4.4 percent reduction exceeds the 4 percent threshold that this program sets for Saxenda reauthorization.
Dietitian input predating treatment and continuing monthly, plus two ongoing activity programmes.

supported_claims: The reauthorization threshold for Saxenda under this program is 4 percent, not 5 percent.
The documented reduction of 4.4 percent exceeds the applicable threshold.
Saxenda has its own named limb in the reauthorization subsection and is not covered by the 'all other appetite suppressants' catch-all the denial relied on.
Continuation of lifestyle modification is documented and is not disputed.
unsupported_claims: That the documented reduction reaches 5 percent.
That the member's response is greater than 4.4 percent.
That the reauthorization criteria impose a BMI or duration requirement.
appeal_ground_truth.correct_next_step: Challenge the determination on the ground that the wrong limb of the reauthorization criterion was applied. Quote the Saxenda limb and show the 4.4 percent reduction against the 4 percent requirement.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: Liraglutide was started on November 10, 2025 at a recorded weight of 227 pounds, a BMI of 35.5 kg/m2.
The recorded weight on May 4, 2026 was 217 pounds, a BMI of 34.0 kg/m2, at a height of 5 feet 7 inches.
The reduction is 10 pounds, or 4.4 percent of baseline.
An interval weight of 221 pounds was recorded on February 9, 2026, with no regain at any point.
The member reached 3 mg daily in December 2025 and has continued without interruption.
The member has seen a dietitian monthly since October 13, 2025, before starting the medication.
The applicable UnitedHealthcare reauthorization threshold for Saxenda is 4 percent of baseline body weight.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The member has lost 5 percent or more of baseline body weight.
Saxenda falls under the 'all other appetite suppressants' limb of the reauthorization criterion.
The applicable threshold is 3 percent, which belongs to Qsymia.
The member completed a six-month supervised weight management program.
The reauthorization criteria require a minimum BMI or a minimum duration of therapy.
